prediction: Scene served: Other blobs are the climate (herds graze patches; blobs respond to the food landscape), with Boom and bust. Defaults (the E88 defaults arm): population mean 67, pop > min 0/8, food energy per 1k 370, fed median lifespan about 4300, floor episodes about 13, predators at end 0/8, prey types 1.75. herds0: population mean 90-110 (E79: 93 herd-free), pop > min 0-2/8, food energy/1k 405-460, fed life +0-5%, floor episodes 10-13, predators 0-1/8, prey types 2.0-2.5. food15 (foodRegrowPerArea 0.09, the cleanest single supply lever: items per tick per area, spawned through the patches, with maxFood only a cap): population mean 85-110, pop > min 0-2/8, food energy/1k 445-520, fed life +3-8%, floor episodes 10-13, predators 0-1/8, prey types 2.0-2.5. herds0-food15: population mean 120-170, pop > min 2-5/8, food energy/1k 500-590, fed life +5-10%, floor episodes 6-11, predators 0-2/8, prey types 2.3-3.0. food20 (0.12): population mean 110-150, pop > min 1-4/8, food energy/1k 520-630, floor episodes 8-12, predators 0-1/8, prey types 2.0-2.8. Interaction: if the herd effect (herds0 minus defaults) is smaller under more food (herds0-food15 minus food15 is below herds0 minus defaults), it is food competition; if it is unchanged or larger it is blocking or trampling. Expected: about half the effect, so competition is the larger part with a trampling and blocking residue. Failure gate: no arm lifts the population mean above 150 or pop > min to 4/8, so neither herds nor food supply explains the thin world and the cause is elsewhere (births, disease, floor); a food arm whose food energy/1k does not rise at least 10% means maxFood or patch stock caps the supply and the lever is invalid. Added before the run, no numeric prediction: food15-cap (foodRegrowPerArea 0.09 with maxFood 2400), to test whether maxFood caps the food arms.
